title: Kitchen Lab measured olive oil
summary: Carry the bottle to a graduated cup, tilt to measure, level to stop, and carry the exact recipe amount into the pan. Underfilled and overfilled measures can be returned without changing the saved cook.

checks: The oil ingredient card opens the measuring routine without recording an oil addition.
Move ingredients uses the measured-oil flow too. Tilting fills the 3D cup and leveling stops flow; partial measures cannot enter the pan and can be returned without changing the cook.
Exactly 15 mL can be carried into the pan for two servings. Only the final transfer records the canonical oil action; native provenance survives reload.
An overfilled cup is visibly above the recipe line, cannot silently add an automatic recipe dose, and can be returned for another attempt.
The cup target doubles to 30 mL for four servings, and the measured transfer records the scaled recipe quantity.
The native keyboard shortcut focuses a one-milliliter control. The same exact measure enables an equivalent oil transfer and keeps simulated time unchanged.
The illustrated bottle supports actual tilt-and-hold gestures. Escape stops flow, and a fresh cook clears an unrecorded measure even when no cooking action has been taken.
Picking up the bottle pauses a running cook. Cancelling the carry leaves saved cooking state and evidence unchanged.
Real phone touch fills, levels and carries the measured cup into the pan. The page fits 390px and passes accessibility checks.
The pan quest opens oil measurement on the native bench and through keyboard controls; choosing a step never adds oil automatically.
Replay and finished cooks expose no leftover practice measure and cannot add oil.
Narrow screens and forced colors pass. Graphics loss cancels a native carry and leaves the measuring cup usable through text controls.
Six illustrated ingredients expose state-derived observations without changing recipe evidence.
Ingredient activities select the matching 3D tool and camera; the field-guide shortcut exits expanded mode with useful focus.
The detailed oil bottle fills a marked cup; carrying the measured oil into the pan changes both the cook and the live observation.
Both whole-produce models transition to measured slices after a real cut gesture.
Recipe quantities, narrow-screen layout, and text-view controls remain available.
A measured splash updates the saved-water observation and stays accurate after reload.
Ingredient actions follow live text-view changes; high-contrast colors remain readable.
Carrying and pressing without lifting records no sample, action, time or food change.
Escape, lateral scrubbing and pointer cancellation restore the scene without saving incomplete evidence.
A complete carry, press, lift and release records exactly one canonical pasta inspection and reveals its actual hard core.
Native provenance and observation survive reload. Cooking marks the saved sample stale; a fresh check retains the previous label and time.
Tender and overcooked checks use the engine observation, with corresponding recorded core and compression visuals.
The native keyboard shortcut focuses the existing food check and records equivalent inspection evidence without advancing time.
Picking up a fork pauses a running kitchen and holds cooking time during the inspection.
The sauce quest leads learners into the native fork routine when a pasta check is needed, without automatically recording a check.
Replay reveals only checks recorded by its selected frame and locks native cooking actions.
A real touch carry, press and lift records a sample at 390px; touch cancellation saves nothing and the page fits the viewport.
The complete routine works at 320px and in forced colors. Graphics loss cancels a carry and leaves the equivalent food check usable.
Native pour animation captured during actual flow; the practice draft leaves cooking state unchanged.
Returning the cup opens the bottle, empties only the practice draft, and restores the bench pose.
